Daily Digest · Computer Science

AI Agents Escape the Lab, Build Real Robots

Today's submissions reveal a decisive shift: AI systems are moving from benchmarks to physical reality. RoboBuilder demonstrates that simulation alone fails—agents must learn from real-world video feedback to design functioning robots. Meanwhile, MLE agents autonomously optimize recommendation systems at industry scale, and Colombo charts a frontier for oracle-based optimization itself. The common thread: agents that close the loop between prediction and consequence.

⚡ Highlighted Findings 4 selected · AI-curated
Robotics
Real Robots Expose Simulation's Fatal Flaw

RoboBuilder builds and tests every AI-designed robot on a physical course, not just in simulation. The stunning result: zero out of 15 simulation-passing designs succeeded in reality, forcing agents to learn simulator corrections from live video feedback.

Agents that learn from real-world video feedback improve dramatically—no simulator-only design crossed the physical course.
Nehme, Nam, Srinivasan, Ahmed 2611.23855 PDF
Machine Learning
LLM Agents Now Optimize Production ML Systems

MLE agents autonomously propose, implement, train, and evaluate improvements to large-scale recommendation models—the kind used by real platforms. This moves agentic ML engineering from toy benchmarks to actual industry workflows.

Human-on-the-loop agents can operate the full ML development loop for billion-scale recommendation systems, not just toy tasks.
Li, Liang, Raj 2611.23910 PDF
Computer Vision
Foundation Model Recovers 4D Geometry from Wild Images

π⁴ unifies dense geometry, camera poses, 3D point tracks, and motion recovery from any image collection or video—calibrated or uncalibrated. A single model handles single images, unordered collections, and video sequences with state-of-the-art results.

π⁴ achieves best average rank across diverse geometry benchmarks while recovering both static scene structure and dynamic motion from diverse, uncalibrated input.
Wang, Zhao, Yang, Guo, Dong 2611.23144 PDF
AI Safety
LLMs Fail to Audit Clinical Models Reliably

LLMs promised to explain and audit clinical prediction models by querying them. A blinded test with planted flaws reveals they cannot reliably find deliberately embedded errors—raising serious concerns about their use as model validators.

LLMs failed to detect most planted flaws in clinical models despite having query access, undermining their credibility as automated auditors.
Liu, Yang 2611.24795 PDF

Featured Researcher
GN
Ghadi Nehme
Research Scientist · MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab

Nehme's work bridges simulation and reality by forcing AI systems to learn from physical world feedback. RoboBuilder exemplifies this philosophy: rather than trusting simulators, the system measures the gap between prediction and outcome on actual robots. This methodological rigor—treating reality as the ultimate arbiter—represents a critical shift in how we validate AI agents before deployment.
